prerequisites: Kinematic and dynamic analysis of machines (Theory of Machines and Mechanisms from 2nd year)
High-level programming (Industrial Computing and Communications from 3rd year)

learning_outcomes.text: Capacity for modeling and simulation of systems
Knowledge of automatic regulation and control techniques and their application to industrial automation
Application of knowledge of principles and applications of robotic systems
Applied knowledge of industrial computing and communications
Knowledge about the fundamentals of automatisms and control methods
understand the multidisciplinary nature of robotics and its implications in the design and implementation of robotic systems
represent and analytically describe the movement of a robot
analyze and model the different subsystems that make up a robot
solve computational robotics problems: localization, maps, motion planning, etc.
design a robotic system using the Model-Based Design (MBD) methodology
know and be able to apply robot programming tools
evaluate the convenience of a robotic solution to solve a given problem

syllabus_topics: Part 1: fundamentals. Introduction: history, characteristics and future of industrial robotics.
Part 2: orientations. Analytical representation of movement in 3D.
Part 3: robot kinematics. The manipulator robot: analytical description, dynamics and control.

assessment_methods.method: Experimental work (individual presentation and active participation)

assessment_rules: The objective test and the experimental work must both be passed individually to pass the course. If both are passed, their respective weights in the final grade will be 75% for the objective test and 25% for the experimental work, though this may vary by mutual agreement with the student depending on the complexity of the experimental work. In extraordinary calls and for differentiated evaluation, the grade will depend exclusively on the objective test.
